findings.title: Verdict response carries no dimension fields — completeness/consistency/compliance must be derived from three other endpoints
findings.evidence: POST /verdict before and after verification returned only {verdict, reason, blocking_pending, blocking_exceptions, pending_verification, advisory} (captured in captures.json pass_b.verdict_before / verdict_after). The report's dimension panels are labeled DERIVED and join GET readout (states), POST detect-exceptions (R1/R2/R3) and the catalog rule table.
findings.impact: Any dashboard showing the product's three stated dimensions needs 3+ API reads per file; there is no single readiness-shape payload.

findings.title: Engine has no severity concept on findings
findings.evidence: POST detect-exceptions returned 0 conflicts / 0 missing_signatures / 0 overdue, and each finding shape carries only field/values/document_ids/reason-style strings (schemas.py ConflictFinding/MissingSignatureFinding/OverdueRequirementFinding). No severity or confidence field exists on any finding.
findings.impact: Triage UIs must invent their own severity mapping; the report's Severity column is report-authored, not engine output.

findings.title: Requirement-to-document resolution is only observable through review-queue state_reason, not a per-document endpoint
findings.evidence: After reconcile, GET review-queue pending_verification items each carried state_reason 'Matched document #<id> (<TYPE>)' for all 6 received requirements (pass_b.queue_mid); GET /documents/{id} exposes no back-reference to the requirement it satisfied.
findings.impact: Auditing why a document counted toward a requirement requires reading the whole review queue; there is no doc-centric resolution view.

findings.title: Requirement.owner is never populated — owner accountability is not engine data
findings.evidence: Readout requirements (pass_b.readout_mid / readout_after) expose only requirement_key/type/status/state/overdue; no owner field exists in ReadoutRequirement. The report's Owner column is labeled DERIVED and mapped from requirement type + source.
findings.impact: Work-routing/ownership views cannot be built from the API today; adding owner to the catalog rule would be the natural fix.

findings.title: Verdict pending_verification (5 keys) disagrees with review-queue pending_verification bucket (6 items) by design
findings.evidence: Before verification: verdict.pending_verification = [agent_visual_inspection, ca_nhd, ca_spq, ca_tds, listing_agreement] (blocking statuses only) while the review-queue bucket held 6 items — the queue includes prelim_title_report (RECOMMENDED), which the verdict instead lists under advisory. Captured in pass_b.verdict_before vs pass_b.queue_before.
findings.impact: Consumers reconciling the two lists will see a 1-item gap whenever a non-blocking requirement has evidence; not a bug, but an undocumented-looking semantics trap.

findings.severity: tooling (this report's runner, not the engine)
findings.title: Attempt 1 of the journey run was aborted by a runner bug after all stages completed; Pass B was re-measured under a fresh idempotency key
findings.evidence: run_journey.py crashed with KeyError 'w' while scoring (a forbid_win ground-truth check declared an end-anchor instead of a width). Attempt 1 had already verified all 6 requirements on listing file 17 (idempotency key e2e-journey-2026-10-07-passB), which would have made a replayed 'verdict before' show a post-verification state. The measured run therefore used e2e-journey-2026-10-07-passB-attempt2 (listing file 18); the Pass A key was reused because Pass A never verifies and file 16's state is naturally pre-verification.
findings.impact: No engine impact. The captures on this page are entirely from the attempt-2 run; attempt 1 left listing files 16 (passA) and 17 (passB, verified) in the local demo database.

n8n's REST executions API returns 401 without N8N_API_KEY, so execution outcome was probed by reading execution_entity from /home/node/.n8n/database.sqlite inside the n8n container (docker exec, sqlite readOnly) — probe host and candidate log are in captures.json pass_a.
The container's effective settings are llm_provider=mock, llm_prompt_version=v2, llm_model=gpt-6-luna — the model id is an inherited compose env default that the mock provider never calls.
Pre-reconcile review-queue showed all 6 documents unmatched with reason no_evidence and zero property_mismatch, confirming property identity resolution passed for every document.
Pass A total webhook round-trip was 1754 ms for the full 6-document orchestrated journey (upload -> classify -> extract per document plus reconcile/detect/verdict/readout).
